title: Parking a distance number puts your click at its centre, not at its edge
goal: Measuring a distance takes three clicks, and the third click parks the number. Click into the gap just under a button and half the number grows back up toward the button, because your click becomes the middle of the pill rather than the near edge of it. So the number ends up closer to the thing you measured than the spot you actually pointed at. Worth deciding whether the click should mean the near edge of the number instead.
notes: Found while fixing a-measurement-number-keeps-clear-of-the-edge-it. NOT a bug: the app obeys the click. The readout centres on labelAnchor, which is the head line, and the third click sets headOffset (CanvasMeasure.swift, measureHeadOffset). Evidence: Scripts/playtest/distance-three-clicks.json clicks [357, 840] to park the number on a button whose bottom edge is at y=816, i.e. 24 px of gap, and the pill (43 px tall) centres there, so it ends 2.5 px under the edge. That picture is queue/audits/2026-09-08-distance-three-clicks.png, the one that filed the clearance task. Size and Gap mode are unaffected: they place their own head and now stand off by half the pill height plus half the chip (MeasureBuilder.clearingHeadOffset). This is a UX judgement about what a click means, so it wants a decision card rather than a unilateral change.
acceptance: A decision card asks whether the third click means the centre of the number or its near edge, with a picture of each
Whichever way it goes, clicking a spot just off an element leaves the number where a person expected to put it
The existing distance walk still passes

Reproduced first. Ran Scripts/playtest/distance-three-clicks.json with Screen Recording granted: the 123 px readout under Save Changes has its top edge on the button's bottom edge (click 24 pt below the edge, pill 43 tall, so 2.5 pt of air). Picture: queue/decisions/...-today.png. The task's reading of the code is right, and the app is obeying the click.

Adversarial review before building. The deeper problem is not the arithmetic, it is that the number was INVISIBLE while you aimed: the placement preview drew the thin squared U and a dot on the head, and the pill only appeared on the commit. Nobody can aim 'half the height of a number that is not on screen yet'. So the shortest thing that delivers most of the value is to show the real readout under the pointer, whichever way the semantics question goes.

Shipped that part (commit 'See the number you are parking before you click'). New MeasureRasterizer.readoutPill/chipFootprint bake the same pill the composite draws; CanvasMeasure holds it under the pointer during .secondPlaced, planned with MeasureLabelPlanner exactly as the commit plans it so nothing jumps. Baked once per placement (span is fixed by then), and the ~23 ms subject detection is cached on the feet, which cannot move while the head is aimed. Review of the built thing found the blue head dot sitting in the middle of the number; removed it, the pill marks the spot now. Tests: Scripts/test.sh green, 5269 tests, 5 new in MeasureReadoutPreviewTests. Walks: distance-*, measure-*, redline-* all pass. New walk Scripts/playtest/distance-parking-preview.json holds the aiming moment and the landing.

Considered a fourth option and dropped it: 'always use the standard standoff, the click only picks the side'. It cannot work for Distance. clearingHeadOffset measures from the FOOT line, and a Distance caliper's feet are wherever you clicked (here, the middle of the button), not on the element's edge the way Size and Gap put them. Tried it: the pill still overlapped the button by ~8 pt.

Blocked on the decision 'When you click to park a distance number, which part of the number should land on your click?' with three real photographs of the app, one per option (today / near edge / never crowds). Option c was produced by inflating the caliper's detected subjects by subjectClearance before planReadout in EditorState.addMeasure, a one-line change reverted after the capture; that is the implementation if c is picked. Option a is marked declines. Recommended c.
Audit for the shipped slice: queue/audits/2026-09-08-distance-parking.json, with real window captures (Screen Recording granted).

Waiting on the decision 'When you click to park a distance number, which part of the number should land on your click?' (three real pictures of the app, one per option; c recommended). The decidable half shipped: the number now rides under the pointer while you aim the third click, so where it will sit is visible before you commit. Tests green, distance/measure/redline walks pass, audit at queue/audits/2026-09-08-distance-parking.json.
decision "When you click to park a distance number, which part of the number should land on your click?" resolved: Your click is the middle, but it never crowds what you measured

Resumed on the resolved decision: option c, "your click is the middle, but it never crowds what you measured". Re-read queue/decisions/parking-a-distance-number-puts-your-click-at-its-when-you-click-to-park-a-distanc.json before starting; status resolved, choice c.

Adversarial review before building. The catch in c is that the app can only stand off from something it can SEE, so a click into a gap the detector missed still centres. Accepted: the preview under the pointer already shows where the number will sit, so a non-slide is visible rather than a surprise. Also checked the other direction: inflating subjects inside MeasureLabelPlanner.plan for every caller was tempting (one place, one rule) but it moves Size and Gap numbers too - plannerLeavesAMeasurementWithOpenSpaceExactlyWhereItWas fails, and those modes already keep the air via clearingHeadOffset. So the growth belongs to the caller that lacks a computed standoff: the caliper you place by hand.

Shipped. New MeasureContent.subjectsWithClearance(_:) in PhotonzCore grows the detected subjects by subjectClearance; wired into EditorState.addMeasure (the commit), CanvasMeasure.layoutMeasureReadoutPreview (the number riding under the pointer, so the preview and the commit agree and nothing jumps) and EditorState.commitMeasureEndpoints (a handle drag replans with the same manners). Size and Gap untouched. Design note added to docs/design/next-measure.md.

Tests, written first: 6 in MeasureLabelPlacementTests (premise, slide below, slide above, open space unchanged, nothing detected, the clearance grows on every side) and 5 in MeasureCalloutClearanceTests on the real capture, including a sweep over every gap on the capture proving the request for air never leaves a number worse off - where a clear spot exists it takes it, where none does it keeps the classic centred spot. Scripts/test.sh green: 5614 tests.

Verified in the app, not just in tests. Screen Recording granted. distance-three-clicks and distance-parking-preview: the pill lands in exactly the spot the preview showed (no jump), the head bar stays on the click, and the air under the Save Changes button went from 2.5 pt to about 30 pt. Walks run: distance-* (2), caliper-* (5), measure-*/size-* (7), redline-* (3), all 17 pass. Audit with both real captures at queue/audits/2026-09-12-distance-parking-clearance.json.

Review of the built thing: with the new caliper still selected, the blue head handle now draws on the pill's top edge rather than hiding under the pill, because the number no longer centres on the bar. Left as is - it is the existing rule for any relocated readout (aRelocatedReadoutLeavesTheHeadHandleBare) and the dot is the thing you grab to change the standoff - but it is in the audit's rough list for the user to judge.

The resolved decision (option c) is built: a hand-placed distance number still centres on your click, but when that would leave it against the element you measured it slides out and keeps the same air Size and Gap keep, with the caliper's bar left on the click. MeasureContent.subjectsWithClearance in PhotonzCore, wired into the commit, the preview under the pointer and a handle drag. Verified in the app with Screen Recording granted: the air under the Save Changes button went from 2.5 pt to about 30 pt and the pill lands exactly where the preview showed it. Scripts/test.sh green (5614 tests, 11 new); 17 distance/caliper/measure/size/redline walks pass. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-12-distance-parking-clearance.json. Commit 9fe67b41.
